title: Two factorizations of the suspension comparison of a pushout square
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be pointed infinity categories, modeled by simplicial sets with fillers for every inner horn, and each having a zero object $0$ that is both initial and terminal. A standard simplex is the nerve of a finite ordered set; an inner horn is the union of its codimension-one faces except one face that is neither first nor last. Assume $\mathcal C$ admits finite colimits and $\mathcal D$ admits finite limits, all in the mapping-space sense; finite diagrams are indexed by simplicial sets with finitely many nondegenerate simplices [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Write $\Sigma X=0\coprod_X0$ in $\mathcal C$ and $\Omega Y=0\times_Y0$ in $\mathcal D$. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be reduced, meaning that $F(0)$ is a zero object. For each coherent commutative square $\tau:\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$, with vertices and edges $(W\to X,W\to Y,X\to Z,Y\to Z)$, let
$$a_\tau:F(W)\longrightarrow P_\tau=F(X)\times_{F(Z)}F(Y)$$
be its canonical pullback comparison. Applying $F$ to the suspension square defines $\eta_V:F(V)\to\Omega F(\Sigma V)$ for each $V$. Naturality defines
$$u_\tau:P_\tau\longrightarrow Q_\tau=\Omega F(\Sigma X)\times_{\Omega F(\Sigma Z)}\Omega F(\Sigma Y).$$
Under the canonical identification $Q_\tau\simeq\Omega(F(\Sigma X)\times_{F(\Sigma Z)}F(\Sigma Y))$, if $\tau$ is a pushout square, there exists a map
$$\theta_\tau:P_\tau\longrightarrow\Omega F(\Sigma W)$$
with specified homotopies
$$\theta_\tau a_\tau\simeq\eta_W,\qquad (\Omega a_{\Sigma\tau})\theta_\tau\simeq u_\tau.$$
Here $\Sigma\tau$ is the square obtained by applying suspension to every vertex and arrow. No equivalence hypothesis on the maps $\eta_V$ is assumed.
